Code is on `main` (a4892dc); the tables below are produced by `scripts/aggregate_all.sh` and reach `paper-repo` `results/` with the next delivery (job running; I will say when). Numbers here are from the same code on the current tables.
  > 
  > **1. C8 population.** `c8_cov` now carries a `population` column: `figure: Bernoulli, true graph, mechanisms a-f, no sanity/convex` (design bern, `edge_noise_q == 0`, runs not `sanity_*`/`convex_*`, mechanisms a-f; 1800 cells), `all Bernoulli cells` (1974) and `cluster designs` (396, cluster bootstrap). Per-bin HC0 means of the figure population: 0.925, 0.919, 0.868, 0.668, 0.158 for |bias|/SD bins (0, .25], (.25, .5], (.5, 1], (1, 2], (2, inf), i.e. your numbers; overall 0.736 (HC0) and 0.735 (unit bootstrap). The old pooled values (0.929 ... 0.155) are the `all Bernoulli cells` rows. The report should quote the `figure` rows.
  > 
  > **2. Absolute held-out R^2 of log RMSE.** New `diagnostic_absolute.csv` (long format: `variant`, `holdout` = mechanism|family, `predictor`, `group` = pooled or the held-out group, `held_out_r2`, bootstrap `ci_lo/ci_hi` over groups for the pooled row, `n_cells`). Predictors: combined score, best degree benchmark, variance-only (L), controls only (log n, log sigma^2) and constant only (mean of the training groups). R^2 uses the variance about the grand mean of the evaluated cells, as the gains do, so the held-out constant is slightly negative. Per-cell held-out predictions are in `diagnostic.csv`: `pred_logrmse_constant`, `pred_logrmse_controls` (leave-one-mechanism-out) and `..._lofo`. Pre-registered variant, pooled, 2178 cells: leave-one-mechanism-out combined 0.319, best benchmark (n p(1-p)/d) 0.286, variance-only 0.253, controls-only 0.011, constant -0.049; leave-one-family-out combined 0.341, best benchmark 0.350, variance-only 0.249, controls-only 0.073, constant -0.028. (Intervals in the file come from the full 2000-draw bootstrap after the delivery.) Your dotted line at the mean log RMSE is therefore not the held-out constant (about -0.03 to -0.05 below it in R^2); use the per-cell columns.
  > 
  > **3. `or_fit`.** It is a real property, not a fitting defect. Reproduced in `analysis/or_fit_check.py` (core SBM n = 3000, p = 0.5, s = 0.5, four graph draws x 300 assignments, per-assignment profile recorded): at d = 5 (c) `or_fit` equals `or_known` (RMSE 0.087 vs 0.087), at d = 20 it is 0.549 vs 0.233, at d = 80 2.00 vs 0.54; (e) 0.34 vs 0.14, 0.64 vs 0.32, 1.05 vs 0.64 (DM about 0.50 throughout). Cause: the SSE profile over the shape parameter is almost flat (median relative SSE range over the grid 0.3% at d = 5, 0.05% at d = 20, 0.01% at d = 80 for (c)), so the minimiser lands at the ends of the grid (59% and 86% of draws at d = 20 and 80 for (c), at kappa = 0.5 or 8; 82% and 86% for (e), at rho = 0.1 or 0.8), and the corner contrast extrapolated from a wrong shape is far off (RMSE with the shape held fixed at each grid value, d = 80 (c): 0.42 at kappa = 0.5 ... 2.8 at kappa = 8). It is the extrapolation problem again: at large d the exposure fraction concentrates near p, so the shape cannot be identified from the observed support while the estimand lives at the corners. The row is as computed; the caption should say "oracle functional form, shape parameter fitted by profile over a grid; the profile is flat on the observed support so the fit is unstable at d >= 20". For (d) the grid contains the true theta, so the two rows coincide in that cell.
